My Price is My Life | Setting Sail with Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley and James O’Keefe Episode #4

Whistleblower Jodi O’Malley comes aboard the Lucky Charm III to share what her life’s been like since she heroically exposed how the federal government was handling (and allegedly hiding) adverse reactions to the COVID-19 vaccine.

In 2021, Jodi was a nurse at the Phoenix Indian Medical Center, a facility under the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). She tells James how the Holy Spirit prompted her to hit “record” while her concerned colleagues, including physicians, were discussing patients they believed were suffering adverse effects from the vaccine, reactions that weren't being formally reported. Thus, igniting Jodi’s ongoing advocacy in nursing.

Jodi also shares other challenging moments in her life that strengthened her faith and trust in God, leading her to the work and mission she’s tackling now.

➡️ Hong Kong man loses HK$13 million in fake crypto investment app scam 

🌐 A Hong Kong man in his 70s has lost more than HK$13 million ($1.67 million) after a self-described cryptocurrency investment expert contacted him through WhatsApp and directed him to a fake trading app. The latest case began when the elderly man received an unsolicited WhatsApp message from someone claiming to be a cryptocurrency investment expert from Singapore. The person introduced him to what was presented as a crypto platform offering favorable exchange rates, low fees and withdrawals at any time.

‼️ Following the instructions he received, the man opened a cryptocurrency wallet and purchased Tether (USDT) and Ethereum (ETH). He was then told to download an investment application supplied by the scammer and transfer the cryptocurrency to designated wallet addresses as investment capital.

📣 Seeing his account balance rise inside the app, the victim became less suspicious and continued sending more cryptocurrency to the wallets provided by the scammer. The fraud only became clear when he tried to withdraw his funds and was repeatedly prevented from doing so under different pretexts. By the time the victim realized the investment platform was fraudulent, his losses had exceeded HK$13 million.

🔊 Intelligence Ministry vows to pursue assassins of Sunni cleric

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Intelligence Ministry has strongly condemned the assassination of Molavi Yousef Gorgij, the Sunni prayer leader of the Mohammad Rasulollah Mosque in Zahedan, saying the killing will not undermine national and religious unity.

In a message issued following Gorgij’s assassination, the ministry described him as a prominent religious scholar and advocate of unity who had worked throughout his life to promote solidarity, national cohesion, Islamic brotherhood, and rapprochement among Islamic schools of thought.
​
“The blood of a martyr is a beacon guiding the way toward the unity and solidarity of the Iranian nation,” the ministry said.
​
It described the assassination as a “bitter loss” for the people of Sistan and Baluchestan and all those committed to Iran’s security, unity, and dignity, stressing that targeting such figures constitutes an attack not only on individuals but also on society’s security, unity, and social capital.
​
The ministry vowed to continue efforts to identify and legally deal with those responsible for the assassination, as well as its perpetrators, masterminds, and supporters.
​
“Undoubtedly, the path of this dear martyr in defending the discourse of the unity of the Islamic Revolution will continue,” the ministry said.
​
“Let the enemies of Iran’s Islamic security and unity know that terrorism can never silence the idea of unity; rather, it strengthens the Islamic approach of solidarity and brotherhood,” it added.
​
The ministry also called on the Iranian people, particularly residents of Sistan and Baluchestan, not to allow the blood of those killed to become a pretext for division between Sunni and Shia Muslims.
​
Gorgij was shot dead by unidentified armed men outside his home in Zahedan on Monday evening. He was known for his activities against divisive elements and Zionism.

The tool is still in beta. xAI collects feedback, while letters in complex fonts and small sizes can still float.
